paragraphs: When used in this report, unless otherwise indicated, "Nurix," "Company," "we," "us" and "our" refers to Nurix Therapeutics, Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries.

We are a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development and commercialization of targeted protein degradation medicines, the next frontier in innovative drug design aimed at improving treatment options for patients with cancer and inflammatory diseases. Powered by a fully artificial intelligence (AI)-integrated discovery engine capable of tackling any protein class, and coupled with leading ligase expertise, Nurix has built a significant advantage in translating the science of protein degradation into clinical advancements with the aim of establishing degrader-based treatments at the forefront of patient care. Our wholly owned, clinical stage pipeline includes three investigational drug candidates designed with the goal to be first-in-class or best-in-class therapeutics: bexobrutideg (NX-5948), a highly selective degrader of Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK); zelebrudomide (NX-2127), a dual degrader of BTK and transcription factors IKZF1(Ikaros) and IKZF3 (Aiolos); and NX-1607, an inhibitor of Casitas B-lineage lymphoma proto-oncogene B (CBL-B), an E3 ligase that regulates activation of multiple immune cell types including T cells and NK cells. We are also advancing multiple potentially first-in-class or best-in-class degraders and degrader antibody conjugates (DACs) in our preclinical pipeline. Our partnered drug discovery pipeline consists of a clinical stage degrader of IRAK4 (NX-0479/GS-6791), a preclinical stage degrader of STAT6, currently in investigational new drug application (IND), enabling studies, and multiple currently undisclosed targets under collaboration agreements with Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Gilead), Sanofi S.A. (Sanofi) and Pfizer Inc. (Pfizer). Within these collaborations, we retain certain options for co-development, co-commercialization and profit sharing in the United States for multiple drug candidates. Both our wholly owned and partnered pipelines are driven by our DEL-AI discovery engine which employs advanced machine learning to enable all aspects of discovery, starting with DNA encoded library (DEL) hit-finding and degrader design, followed by automated chemistry synthesis and direct-to-biology screening and optimization, to rapidly generate degraders and DACs as new chemical entity drug candidates. By leveraging hundreds of billions of DEL compound binding signatures derived from thousands of DEL affinity screens collected from a diverse set of highly validated protein targets, our DEL-AI engine can prospectively identify binders as starting points for drug discovery for virtually any pharmaceutically relevant target.

Our wholly owned pipeline of drug candidates comprises three clinical stage oncology programs and multiple preclinical stage Targeted Protein Degrader (TPD) and Degrader Antibody Conjugate (DAC) programs spanning the therapeutic areas of oncology, inflammation and immunology. Our partnered pipeline further expands our reach into rheumatoid arthritis and Type 2 inflammation, as well as solid tumor oncology via multiple undisclosed programs. This combination of wholly owned and partnered portfolios across a range of indications and modalities demonstrates our ability to discover and advance novel medicines, many of which selectively target disease proteins previously thought to be undruggable. Our portfolio of targeted protein degraders of the B‑cell signaling protein BTK comprises bexobrutideg, an investigational, orally bioavailable, highly selective BTK degrader for the treatment of relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies and potentially autoimmune diseases, and zelebrudomide, an investigational, orally bioavailable degrader that simultaneously degrades BTK and two well-characterized cereblon neosubstrates IKZF1 (Ikaros) and IKZF3 (Aiolos) that are clinically validated transcription factor targets for relapsed or refractory B‑cell malignancies.

Status of Bexobrutideg: We are currently conducting a Phase 2 study of bexobrutideg in patients with relapsed or refractory CLL having failed three previous lines of therapy, specifically a covalent BTK inhibitor (cBTKi), a BCL2 inhibitor (BCL2i) and a non-covalent BTK inhibitor (ncBTKi). This study is designed as a potentially pivotal trial for Accelerated Approval in the United States and commenced in October 2025 upon agreement with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the use of the 600mg, once daily dose of bexobrutideg as determined by our Phase 1b study of both a 200mg and a 600mg dose in patients in accordance with the FDA's Project Optimus. In January 2024, the FDA granted Fast Track designation for bexobrutideg for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) after at least two lines of therapy, including a BTK inhibitor and a B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL2) inhibitor. In November 2024, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) granted Priority Medicine (PRIME) designation for bexobrutideg in CLL or SLL after at least a BTK inhibitor and a BCL-2 inhibitor. In December 2024, the FDA granted Fast Track designation for bexobrutideg for the treatment of adult patients with Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia (WM) after at least two lines of therapy, including a BTK inhibitor.

Status of Zelebrudomide: We are currently conducting a Phase 1a/1b dose-escalation and cohort expansion study of zelebrudomide in patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies. We previously initiated Phase 1b expansion cohorts for patients with relapsed CLL, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). Enrollment was paused in 2023 due to a partial clinical hold stemming from a manufacturing change designed to produce a chirally controlled form of zelebrudomide. Enrollment of new patients in this clinical trial recommenced in August 2024 following resolution of the partial hold by the FDA. Dose escalation with the new drug form is ongoing with a focus on patients with aggressive forms of B-cell lymphoma, such as DLBCL and MCL.

In addition to our BTK degrader portfolio, we are also advancing a novel immune-oncology inhibitor of the E3 ligase CBL-B. CBL-B is a RING-type E3 ligase that regulates the activation of multiple immune cell types including T cells and NK cells through protein degradation. NX-1607 is an orally bioavailable inhibitor of CBL-B that has the potential to reduce T cell anergy and promote anti-cancer immune cell activity. NX-1607 is currently being explored in a variety of solid tumor indications.

Status of NX-1607: We are currently conducting a Phase 1a/1b dose-escalation and cohort expansion study of NX-1607 in patients with a range of oncology indications. This study also includes a cohort within the Phase 1a dose escalation study testing NX-1607 in combination with paclitaxel, a taxane chemotherapy commonly used across a range of relapsed and refractory solid tumor indications. In 2022, NX-1607 was awarded an Innovation Passport from the United Kingdom (UK) Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency to accelerate time to market and facilitate patient access to novel drugs to treat serious and life-threatening diseases.

In addition to our clinical stage drug candidates, we are advancing multiple preclinical-stage programs within our protein degradation portfolio, both on our own and with partners, by developing new targeted protein degraders and degrader antibody conjugates for several therapeutic indications that currently lack treatment options or where current therapies are ineffective. These existing and future programs have the potential to provide patients with better options in therapeutic indications with significant unmet needs, including cancer, inflammation, autoimmunity and other challenging therapeutic areas.

We have entered into several revenue generating collaborations with large biopharmaceutical companies, including Gilead, Sanofi and Pfizer, to leverage our DEL-AI platform for drug discovery. As of November 30, 2025, we have received a total of $482.0 million in non-dilutive financing from our collaborators, and we are eligible to receive up to $6.1 billion in potential future fees and milestone payments, as well as royalties on future product sales. We retain certain options for co-development, co-commercialization and profit sharing in the United States for multiple drug candidates pursuant to these collaborations.

Our strategy is to discover and develop breakthrough therapies for patients with significant unmet clinical need by developing highly differentiated degrader-based medicines that alter or remove disease-causing or disease-associated biological targets that to date have been ineffectively drugged or have been considered undruggable with existing modalities. The key elements of our strategy are to:

•Advance our lead program, bexobrutideg, into late-stage clinical development in CLL and potentially other B-cell malignancies. Enrollment is ongoing in our Phase 2 clinical trial of bexobrutideg in adults with relapsed or refractory CLL. In 2026, we intend to commence enrollment of a suite of additional trials designed to support the potential future registration of the drug in multiple regulatory jurisdictions. We plan to leverage the Fast Track designation from the FDA in CLL and WM as well as the PRIME designation from the EMA to accelerate the clinical development and registrational path for bexobrutideg in oncology.

•Explore the therapeutic applications of bexobrutideg, for the treatment of patients with diseases caused by inflammation and autoimmunity. BTK mediates signaling downstream of the B-cell receptor (BCR), toll-like receptors (TLRs), and Fc receptors (FcRs), making it an attractive therapeutic target in antibody-mediated autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Targeting BTK can reduce the production of new antibodies and mitigate inflammation induced by a variety of inflammatory signals, addressing key challenges in inflammatory and autoimmune diseases. We believe that bexobrutideg may offer unique advantages over currently available BTK inhibitors in these disease indications by addressing both the enzymatic and scaffold activities of BTK, which are key to its function. In 2025, we expanded the current Phase 1b trial in patients with CLL to include patients who are also suffering from immune-mediated cytopenias such as anemia, a common co-morbidity associated with CLL. In 2026, we may further explore the utility of bexobrutideg in autoimmune and inflammatory diseases with a separate clinical program which will require an IND with a separate division at the FDA.

•Continue development of zelebrudomide through dose escalation with a focus on aggressive lymphomas including MCL and DLBCL. Enrollment of new patients in our Phase 1a/1b clinical trial of NX-2127 has continued in adults with relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies. In 2026, we expect to define doses to enable a Phase 1b cohort expansion.

headings: Risks Related to Our Financial Position and Need for Additional Capital
We have incurred significant losses since our inception. We expect to incur losses over at least the next several years and may never achieve or maintain profitability.
We have never generated revenue from product sales and may never be profitable.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our stockholders, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish rights to our technologies or drug candidates.
Our limited operating history may make it difficult to evaluate the success of our business to date and to assess our future viability.
Risks Related to the Discovery and Development of Our Drug Candidates
If we experience delays or difficulties in enrolling patients in clinical trials, our receipt of necessary marketing approvals could be delayed or prevented.
The manufacture of drugs is complex, and we and our third-party manufacturers are early in our manufacturing efforts.
We may not be successful in our efforts to identify or discover additional potential drug candidates, or in further efforts to expand the breadth of our DEL-AI platform.
We face substantial competition in an environment of rapid technological change, which may result in others discovering, developing or commercializing products before or more successfully than we do.
If we do not achieve our projected development goals in the time frames we expect and announce, the commercialization of our products may be delayed and, as a result, our stock price may decline.
The biopharmaceutical industry is subject to extensive regulatory obligations and policies that are subject to change, including due to judicial challenges.
Risks Related to Dependence on Third Parties

You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and our financial statements and the accompanying notes and the information contained in our other public filings before deciding whether to invest in shares of our common stock. We cannot assure you that any of the events described below will not occur. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties that we are unaware of or that we deem immaterial may also become important factors that adversely affect our business. If any of the following risks occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations, and future prospects could be materially and adversely affected. In that event, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and you could lose all or part of your investment.

Our net loss was $264.5 million and $193.6 million for the fiscal years ended November 30, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of November 30, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $1,003.2 million. To date, we have not generated any revenue from product sales and have financed our operations primarily through our collaborations and sales of our equity interests. We are in the early stages of development of our drug candidates. Our lead drug candidates, bexobrutideg (NX-5948), zelebrudomide (NX-2127) and NX-1607, are in the early stages of clinical development. We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and increasing operating losses for at least the next several years. We anticipate that our operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements will increase substantially if and as we:
•increase enrollment in and further develop our drug candidates bexobrutideg, zelebrudomide and NX-1607 through Phase 1 and Phase 2 clinical trials;
•submit investigational new drug applications (INDs) and initiate clinical trials of our other drug candidates;
•enter advanced clinical development and scale up external manufacturing capabilities to supply clinical trials;
•expand the capabilities of our DEL-AI platform and apply our DEL-AI platform to advance additional drug candidates into preclinical and clinical development;

We have entered into several revenue generating collaborations with large biopharmaceutical companies, including Gilead, Sanofi and Pfizer, to leverage our DEL-AI platform for drug discovery. In aggregate, we have received $482.0 million in non-dilutive financing from our collaborators to date and, as of November 30, 2025, we are eligible to receive up to $6.1 billion in potential future fees and milestone payments, as well as royalties on future product sales. We retain certain options for co-development, co-commercialization and profit sharing in the United States for multiple drug candidates, pursuant to these collaborations.

In June 2019, we entered into a global strategic collaboration agreement with Gilead (as subsequently amended, the Gilead Agreement) to discover, develop and commercialize a pipeline of targeted protein degradation drugs for patients with cancer and other challenging diseases using our DEL-AI platform to identify novel agents that utilize E3 ligases to induce degradation of five specified drug targets. In August 2019 and September 2022, we entered into the First Amendment and the Second Amendment, respectively, to the Gilead Agreement to clarify certain language of the Gilead Agreement. These amendments had no impact on revenue recognition. In February and March 2024, as part of the existing collaboration agreement, Gilead elected to extend the five-year initial research term by two years for certain drug targets (Gilead Research Term Extension). The Gilead Research Term Extension triggered a $15.0 million payment, which we received in the second quarter of fiscal year 2024.

Under the Gilead Agreement, Gilead has the option to license drug candidates directed to up to five targets resulting from the collaboration and is responsible for the clinical development and commercialization of drug candidates resulting from the collaboration. We retain the option to co-develop and co-promote, under a profit share structure, up to two drug candidates in the United States, provided that we may only exercise such option once per licensed product and Gilead retains the right to veto our option selection for any one drug candidate of its choice. The collaboration excludes our current internal protein degradation programs for which we retain all rights, and also excludes our future internal programs, provided that we have distinguished future programs as excluded from the scope of the collaboration. In March 2023, Gilead exercised its option, which did not represent a material right at contract inception, since it was not offered for free or at a discount, to exclusively license one target (Gilead License Option Exercise), the first development candidate resulting from the Gilead Agreement. Pursuant to the Gilead Agreement, we received a license option exercise payment of $20.0 million in April 2023 for the Gilead License Option Exercise. The license to the functional intellectual property and all goods and services related to the Gilead License Option Exercise were transferred during the second quarter of fiscal year 2023.

Over time, Gilead may elect to replace the initial drug targets with other drug targets. For drug targets that are subject to the collaboration, we are obligated to use commercially reasonable efforts to undertake a research program in accordance with a research plan agreed to by the parties and established on a target-by-target basis. We have primary responsibility under the Gilead Agreement for performing preclinical research activities (including target validation, drug discovery, identification or synthesis) pursuant to a research plan. Each party will bear its own costs in the conduct of research activities. Gilead will be responsible for any development, commercialization and manufacturing activities, unless we exercise our co-development and co-promotion option. For those programs that we exercise our option to co-develop and co-promote, we and Gilead will split U.S. development costs as well as U.S. profits and losses evenly, and we will be eligible to receive royalties on net ex-U.S. sales and reduced milestone payments.

Upon signing the Gilead Agreement, Gilead paid us an upfront payment of $45.0 million, plus $3.0 million in additional fees. In addition, from the signing of the Gilead Agreement to November 30, 2025, we have received payments of $47.0 million for research milestones and additional payments, $20.0 million for a license option exercise payment, $15.0 million in research term extension fees and $5.0 million for a clinical milestone payment. As of November 30, 2025, we are eligible to receive up to approximately $1.8 billion in total additional payments based on certain additional fees, payments and the successful completion of certain preclinical, clinical, development and sales milestones. We also are eligible to receive mid-single digit to low tens percentage tiered royalties on annual net sales from any commercial products directed to the optioned collaboration targets, subject to certain reductions and excluding sales in the United States of any products for which we exercise our option to co-develop and co-promote, for which the parties share profits and losses evenly.

Subject to earlier expiration in certain circumstances, the Gilead Agreement expires on a licensed product-by-licensed product and country-by-country basis upon the later of (1) the expiration of the last to expire patent with a valid claim covering the applicable licensed product in the applicable country, (2) the expiration of any regulatory exclusivity for the applicable licensed product in the applicable country or (3) ten years after the first commercial sale of the applicable licensed product in the applicable country covered by the Gilead Agreement, provided that the term for any profit-shared licensed product in the United States will expire upon the expiration or termination of the applicable profit-share term as set forth in an applicable profit-share agreement to be negotiated upon our exercise of our option to co-develop and co-promote such licensed product.

我們是一家臨牀階段的生物製藥公司，專注於發現、開發及商業化針對性蛋白降解藥物，這是創新藥物設計的下一階段，旨在改善癌症及發炎性疾病患者的治療選擇。我們的技術建立在完全整合人工智慧（AI）的發現引擎之上，能處理任何蛋白質類別，並結合領先的配體專業知識，使 Nurix 在將蛋白質降解科學轉化為臨牀進展方面建立了顯著優勢，目標是將基於降解的治療設立為患者照護的先驅。我們的全資擁有、臨牀階段的產品線包括三種研究中藥物候選品，目標為首創或最佳治療選擇：bexobrutideg (NX-5948)，一種高度選擇性的 Bruton's 型酪胺酸 kinase (BTK) 降解物；zelebrudomide (NX-2127)，一種同時降解 BTK 和轉錄因子 IKZF1 (Ikaros) 和 IKZF3 (Aiolos) 的雙重降解物；以及 NX-1607，一種 Casitas B-lineage 淋巴瘤原癌基因 B (CBL-B) 的抑制劑，CBL-B 是一種 E3 結合酶，調控多種免疫細胞類型（包括 T 細胞和 NK 細胞）的活化。我們也在推進多種潛在首創或最佳治療選擇的降解物及降解物抗體結合物（DACs）在我們的臨牀前產品線。我們的合作藥物發現產品線包括一項臨牀階段的 IRAK4 降解物（NX-0479/GS-6791）、一項臨牀前階段的 STAT6 降解物，目前處於新藥申請（IND）階段，並進行研究，以及多個目前未公開的目標，與 Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Gilead)、Sanofi S.A. (Sanofi) 和 Pfizer Inc. (Pfizer) 的合作協議。在這些合作中，我們保留了美國多種藥物候選品的共同開發、共同商業化及利潤分享的選擇權。我們的全資擁有及合作產品線皆由我們的 DEL-AI 發現引擎驅動，該引擎運用先進的機器學習技術，從 DNA 編碼庫（DEL）的命中發現及降解物設計開始，經由自動化化學合成及直接至生物篩選與優化，快速產生降解物及 DACs 作為新化學實體藥物候選品。透過從數千個 DEL 結合親和力篩選中收集的數百億個 DEL 化合物結合簽名，來自多種高度驗證的蛋白質目標，我們的 DEL-AI 引擎可以前瞻性地識別結合物作為藥物發現的起點，適用於幾乎任何藥物相關目標。

我們的全資擁有藥物候選品產品線包括三個臨牀階段的腫瘤學計畫及多個臨牀前階段的目標蛋白質降解物（TPD）及降解物抗體結合物（DAC）計畫，涵蓋腫瘤學、發炎及免疫學的治療領域。我們的合作產品線進一步擴展我們在風濕性關節炎及 Type 2 發炎，以及透過多個未公開計畫的實體腫瘤腫瘤學的影響力。這組合的全資擁有及合作產品線涵蓋多種適應症及治療方式，顯示我們發現及推進新藥物的能力，其中許多藥物選擇性地針對過去認為難以藥物作用的疾病蛋白質。以下圖表總結我們的臨牀及臨牀前產品線及進行中的臨牀研究：

我們的目標蛋白質降解物產品線包括針對 B 細胞信號蛋白 BTK 的降解物，包含 bexobrutideg，一種研究中的口服生物可利用、高度選擇性的 BTK 降解物，用於治療復發或難治性 B 細胞惡性腫瘤及潛在的自身免疫疾病，以及 zelebrudomide，一種研究中的口服生物可利用降解物，同時降解 BTK 和兩個已驗證的 cereblon 新底物 IKZF1 (Ikaros) 和 IKZF3 (Aiolos)，這些是臨牀驗證的轉錄因子目標，用於治療復發或難治性 B 細胞惡性腫瘤。

bexobrutideg 狀況：我們目前正在進行一項 Phase 2 研究，用於治療復發或難治性 CLL（慢性淋巴細胞白血病）患者，這些患者已失敗三種先前的治療方式，特別是共價 BTK 抑制劑（cBTKi）、BCL2 抑制劑（BCL2i）及非共價 BTK 抑制劑（ncBTKi）。此研究設計為美國加速批准的潛在關鍵試驗，並於 2025 年 10 月開始，根據與美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）的協議，使用 600mg、每日一次的 bexobrutideg 劑量，此劑量由我們在 Phase 1b 研究中對 200mg 和 600mg 劑量的患者所確定，符合 FDA 的 Project Optimus 計畫。2024 年 1 月，FDA 授予 bexobrutideg 快速通道指定，用於治療至少接受兩種治療線路的成人 CLL 或 SLL 患者，包括 BTK 抑制劑和 B-cell lymphoma 2（BCL2）抑制劑。2024 年 11 月，歐洲藥物管理局（EMA）授予 bexobrutideg 的 PRIME 指定，用於 CLL 或 SLL 患者，至少接受 BTK 抑制劑和 BCL-2 抑制劑治療。2024 年 12 月，FDA 授予 bexobrutideg 快速通道指定，用於治療至少接受兩種治療線路的成人 Waldenstrom's 巨球蛋白血癥（WM）患者，包括 BTK 抑制劑。

zelebrudomide 狀況：我們目前正在進行一項 Phase 1a/1b 劑量遞增及隊列擴展研究，用於治療復發或難治性 B 細胞惡性腫瘤患者。我們先前已啟動 Phase 1b 的擴展隊列，用於治療復發 CLL、瀰漫大 B 細胞淋巴瘤（DLBCL）及套細胞淋巴瘤（MCL）患者。2023 年因製造過程的變更，設計生產一種手性控制的 zelebrudomide 而導致部分臨牀暫停。2024 年 8 月，經 FDA 解決部分暫停後，此臨牀試驗重新開始納入新患者。使用新藥物形式的劑量遞增持續進行，重點在於治療具有侵略性 B 細胞淋巴瘤形式的患者，如 DLBCL 和 MCL。
除了我們的 BTK 降解物產品線，我們也在推進一種新型免疫腫瘤學抑制劑，針對 E3 結合酶 CBL-B。CBL-B 是一種 RING 型 E3 結合酶，透過蛋白質降解調控多種免疫細胞類型（包括 T 細胞和 NK 細胞）的活化。NX-1607 是一種口服生物可利用的 CBL-B 抑制劑，有潛力減少 T 細胞無反應性並促進抗癌免疫細胞活動。NX-1607 目前正在探索多種實體腫瘤適應症。

NX-1607 狀況：我們目前正在進行一項 Phase 1a/1b 劑量遞增及隊列擴展研究，用於治療多種腫瘤學適應症的患者。此研究也包含一項 Phase 1a 劑量遞增研究中的隊列，測試 NX-1607 與紫杉醇（paclitaxel）的組合療法，紫杉醇是一種常見的稅烷化療藥物，用於治療多種復發和難治性實體腫瘤適應症。2022 年，NX-1607 獲得了英國（UK）藥物及醫療產品監管局的創新通行證，以加速上市時間並促進對治療嚴重及威脅生命的疾病的患者的藥物存取。
除我們臨牀階段的藥物候選品之外，我們正在推動多個預臨牀階段的計畫，這些計畫屬於我們的蛋白質降解產品組合，我們既自行推動，也與合作夥伴共同進行，以開發新的針對性蛋白質降解物與降解抗體結合物，用於治療目前缺乏治療選擇或現有療法無效的多種治療指標。這些現有與未來的計畫有潛力為患有重大未滿足醫療需求的患者提供更好的治療選擇，包括癌症、發炎、自身免疫及其它具有挑戰性的治療領域。

我們已與多家大型生物製藥公司，包括 Gilead、Sanofi 和 Pfizer 籤訂產生收入的合作協議，以利用我們的 DEL-AI 平台進行藥物發現。截至 2025 年 11 月 30 日，我們已從合作夥伴處獲得總計 482.0 百萬美元的非稀釋資金，我們有資格獲得最高達 6.1 十億美元的潛在未來費用與里程碑付款，以及未來產品銷售的版稅。根據這些合作協議，我們保留美國多個藥物候選品的共同開發、共同商業化與利潤分享的選擇權。
我們的策略是透過開發高度差異化的降解基於藥物，以發現並開發突破性療法，用以治療具有重大未滿足臨牀需求的患者，這些藥物能改變或去除導致疾病或與疾病相關的生物標的，而這些標的至今尚未被有效藥物治療或被認為無法使用現有方法進行治療。我們策略的關鍵要素為：

•將我們的領先計畫 bexobrutideg 推進至 CLL 和潛在其他 B 細胞惡性腫瘤的晚期臨牀開發階段。我們在成人復發或難治性 CLL 的 Phase 2 臨牀試驗中持續進行受試者招募。2026 年，我們預計開始招募一系列額外試驗，以支持該藥物未來在多個監管管轄區註冊的潛在可能。我們計畫利用 FDA 的 Fast Track 認可於 CLL 和 WM，以及 EMA 的 PRIME 認可，以加速 bexobrutideg 在腫瘤學領域的臨牀開發與註冊路徑。

•探討 bexobrutideg 在治療由發炎和自身免疫引起的疾病患者的治療應用。BTK 會在 B 細胞受體（BCR）、 Toll-like 受體（TLRs）和 Fc 受體（FcRs）下游傳導訊號，使其成為抗體介導的自身免疫和發炎疾病的有吸引力的治療目標。針對 BTK 可減少新抗體的產生，並緩解由多種發炎訊號引起的發炎，解決發炎和自身免疫疾病中的關鍵挑戰。我們認為 bexobrutideg 可能針對這些疾病指標提供目前可用 BTK 抑製劑所無法提供的獨特優勢，透過同時針對 BTK 的酵素活性與支架活性，這些是 BTK 功能的關鍵。2025 年，我們將目前 CLL 患者的 Phase 1b 試驗擴展至同時患有免疫介導性貧血等免疫相關貧血的患者，貧血是 CLL 常見的共病。2026 年，我們可能進一步探討 bexobrutideg 在自身免疫和發炎疾病中的應用，透過一個獨立的臨牀計畫，這將需要與 FDA 的獨立部門簽署 IND。
•持續開發 zelebrudomide 進行劑量遞增，重點在於侵襲性淋巴瘤，包括 MCL 和 DLBCL。我們在 NX-2127 的 Phase 1a/1b 臨牀試驗中持續招募新的患者，這些患者為復發或難治性 B 細胞惡性腫瘤的成人。2026 年，我們預計確定劑量以啟動 Phase 1b 羣體擴展。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與本年度10-K表報表中出現的財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。如「特別提醒有關未來展望聲明」一節所述，以下討論與分析包含未來展望聲明，這些聲明涉及風險與不確定性，以及假設，這些假設若未能實現或證明為錯誤，可能會導致我們的結果與這些未來展望聲明所表達或暗示的結果有重大差異。導致這些差異的因素包括，但不僅限於，以下所列及「風險因素」一節中所討論的內容。

本公司為一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，專注於發現、開發及商業化針對性蛋白降解藥物，這是創新藥物設計的下一階段，旨在改善癌症及發炎性疾病患者的治療選擇。透過完全整合AI的發現引擎，能處理任何蛋白質類別，並結合領先的配體專業知識，我們已建立在將蛋白質降解科學轉化為臨牀進展的優勢，目標是將基於降解的治療設立為患者照護的先鋒。我們運用我們專有的DEL-AI平台，採用先進的自動化化學合成及直接至生物技術，以快速產生降解劑及降解抗體結合物（DACs），作為第一類或最佳類藥物候選品。我們的全資擁有、臨牀階段的產品組合包括針對Bruton's tyrosine kinase（BTK），一種B細胞訊號蛋白的目標蛋白降解劑，以及抑制Casitas B-lineage淋巴瘤原癌基因B（CBL-B），一種調控多種免疫細胞類型（包括T細胞及NK細胞）活化的E3配體。我們的合作藥物發現產品組合包含多個計畫，根據與Gilead Sciences, Inc.（Gilead）、Sanofi S.A.（Sanofi）及Pfizer Inc.（Pfizer）的合作協議，我們在美國對多種藥物候選品保留共同開發、共同商業化及利潤分享的選擇權。

我們針對B細胞訊號蛋白BTK的目標蛋白降解劑產品組合包括bexobrutideg（NX-5948），一種正在研究中的口服生物可利用、高度選擇性的BTK降解劑，用於治療復發或難治性B細胞惡性腫瘤及潛在的自身免疫疾病，以及zelebrudomide（NX-2127），一種正在研究中的口服生物可利用降解劑，同時降解BTK及兩種已驗證的cereblon新底物IKZF1（Ikaros）及IKZF3（Aiolos），這些是臨牀驗證的轉錄因子目標，用於治療復發或難治性B細胞惡性腫瘤。

bexobrutideg（NX-5948）：我們目前正在進行一項二期研究，針對復發或難治性慢性淋巴細胞白血病（CLL）患者，這些患者已失敗三種先前治療，特別是共價BTK抑制劑（cBTKi）、BCL2抑制劑（BCL2i）及非共價BTK抑制劑（ncBTKi）。此研究設計為美國加速批准的潛在關鍵試驗，並於2025年10月開始，經美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）同意使用600毫克、每日一次的bexobrutideg劑量，此劑量由我們在符合FDA的Project Optimus規定下進行的Phase 1b研究中200毫克及600毫克劑量的患者所確定。2024年1月，美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）授予bexobrutideg針對成人復發或難治性慢性淋巴細胞白血病（CLL）或小淋巴細胞淋巴瘤（SLL）患者，經至少兩線治療後（包括BTK抑制劑及B細胞淋巴瘤2（BCL2）抑制劑）的快速通道指定。2024年11月，歐洲藥物管理局（EMA）授予bexobrutideg在CLL或SLL患者經至少BTK抑制劑及BCL-2抑制劑後的優先藥物（PRIME）指定。2024年12月，FDA授予bexobrutideg針對成人復發或難治性華爾登堡氏巨球蛋白血癥（WM）患者，經至少兩線治療後（包括BTK抑制劑）的快速通道指定。

zelebrudomide（NX-2127）：我們目前正在進行一項Phase 1a/1b劑量遞增及隊列擴展研究，針對復發或難治性B細胞惡性腫瘤患者。我們先前已啟動Phase 1b擴展隊列，針對復發CLL、瀰漫大B細胞淋巴瘤（DLBCL）及套細胞淋巴瘤（MCL）患者。2023年因製造變更設計以生產一種手性控制的zelebrudomide形式，導致臨牀暫停。2024年8月，經FDA解決部分暫停後，此臨牀試驗重新納入新患者。使用新藥物形式的劑量遞增持續進行，重點在於治療具有侵略性B細胞淋巴瘤形式的患者，如DLBCL及MCL。
我們的降解抑制劑計畫包括NX-1607，一種口服生物可利用的CBL-B抑制劑，一種調控多種免疫細胞類型（包括T細胞及NK細胞）活化的E3配體。NX-1607針對免疫腫瘤學指徵。

我們目前正在進行一項Phase 1a/1b劑量遞增及隊列擴展研究，針對NX-1607在一系列腫瘤指徵患者中。此研究也包含在Phase 1a劑量遞增研究中的一個隊列，測試NX-1607與紫杉醇（paclitaxel）的組合，紫杉醇是一種常見的稅烷化療藥物，用於治療多種復發或難治性實體腫瘤指徵。2022年，NX-1607獲英國藥物及醫療產品規範管理局（MHRA）頒發創新通行證，以加速上市時間並促進對治療嚴重且威脅生命的疾病的新型藥物的患者取得。
除了我們的臨牀階段藥物候選品外，我們正在推進多個預臨牀階段計畫，這些計畫在本公司與合作夥伴的共同努力下進行，開發新的目標蛋白降解劑及降解抗體結合物，用於目前缺乏治療選擇或現有治療無效的多種治療指徵。這些現有及未來的計畫有潛力為這些具有重大未滿足需求的治療指徵的患者提供更好的選擇，包括癌症、發炎、自身免疫及其他具有挑戰性的治療領域

本公司已與多家大型生物製藥公司建立多項產生收入的合作關係，包括 Gilead、Sanofi 與 Pfizer，以運用本公司 DEL-AI 平台進行藥物研發。截至目前為止，本公司已從合作夥伴處獲得 482.0 百萬美元之非稀釋資金，截至 2025 年 11 月 30 日，本公司有資格獲得最高達 6.1 十億美元之潛在未來費用與里程碑付款，以及未來產品銷售之版稅。本公司保留針對多項藥物候選品於美國進行共同開發、共同商業化與獲利分享之權利，依據這些合作關係。

2019 年 6 月，本公司與 Gilead（後經修正，稱為 Gilead 協議）簽訂全球戰略合作協議，以運用本公司 DEL-AI 平台，針對癌症及其他困難疾病的患者，發現、開發與商業化一連串針對蛋白質降解之藥物。2019 年 8 月及 2022 年 9 月，本公司分別與 Gilead 簽訂第一修正案與第二修正案，以澄清 Gilead 協議之部分語言。這些修正案對收入認列無影響。2024 年 2 月及 3 月，根據現有合作協議，Gilead 選擇將針對某些藥物目標之五年的初始研究期延長兩年（Gilead 研究期延長），此延長觸發 15.0 百萬美元之付款，本公司於 2024 財年第二季收到該筆付款。

根據 Gilead 協議，Gilead 有權就合作產生之藥物候選品，針對最多五個目標進行授權，並負責合作產生之藥物候選品之臨牀開發與商業化。本公司保留於美國對最多兩項藥物候選品進行共同開發與共同推廣之權利，以獲利分享結構為基礎，但本公司僅能針對每一已授權產品行使此權利一次，且 Gilead 保留對其選擇之任一藥物候選品拒絕本公司選項之權利。此合作不包含本公司目前內部之蛋白質降解計畫，本公司保留所有權利，亦不包含未來內部計畫，但本公司已明確將未來計畫排除於合作範疇之外。2023 年 3 月，Gilead 行使其選項，此選項在合約簽訂時並非重大權利，因其非免費或折扣取得，以獨家授權一個目標（Gilead 授權選項行使），為 Gilead 協議所產生之第一個開發候選品。根據 Gilead 協議，本公司於 2023 年 4 月收到 20.0 百萬美元之選項行使付款，為 Gilead 授權選項行使。與 Gilead 授權選項行使相關之功能性智慧財產權與所有商品與服務於 2023 財年第二季完成轉移。

隨時間推移，Gilead 可能選擇將初始藥物目標替換為其他藥物目標。針對合作之藥物目標，本公司有義務依雙方同意之研究計畫，就每個目標進行商業上合理之努力，執行研究計畫。根據 Gilead 協議，本公司負有主要責任執行預臨牀研究活動（包括目標驗證、藥物研發、識別或合成），依研究計畫進行。雙方各自承擔研究活動之成本。Gilead 將負責任何開發、商業化與製造活動，除非本公司行使共同開發與共同推廣之權利。針對本公司行使共同開發與共同推廣之權利之計畫，本公司與 Gilead 將均分美國之開發成本以及美國之獲利與虧損，本公司亦有資格獲得美國以外之淨銷售額之版稅，以及減少之里程碑付款。

簽訂 Gilead 協議時，Gilead 向本公司支付一筆 upfront 付款 45.0 百萬美元，另加 3.0 百萬美元之額外費用。此外，從簽訂 Gilead 協議至 2025 年 11 月 30 日，本公司已收到 47.0 百萬美元之研究里程碑付款與額外付款，20.0 百萬美元之選項行使付款，15.0 百萬美元之研究期延長費用，以及 5.0 百萬美元之臨牀里程碑付款。截至 2025 年 11 月 30 日，本公司有資格獲得總計約 1.8 十億美元之額外付款，基於某些額外費用、付款以及成功完成某些預臨牀、臨牀、開發與銷售里程碑。本公司亦有資格獲得年淨銷售額之中單位數至低十位數百分比階層版稅，針對任何商業產品所針對之選項合作目標，但需扣除美國銷售之產品，若本公司行使共同開發與共同推廣之權利，雙方將均分獲利與虧損。

除非在特定情況下較早到期，Gilead 協議將根據每個已授權產品及每個國家，於以下情形中較晚者到期：(1) 涵蓋適用已授權產品之適用國家之最後到期之具有有效主張之專利到期，(2) 涵蓋適用已授權產品之適用國家之任何監管獨佔到期，或 (3) 自適用已授權產品在適用國家之首次商業銷售起滿十年，但任何獲利共享之已授權產品在美國之期限將於適用獲利共享期限到期或終止時到期，此期限將根據本公司行使共同開發與共同推廣之權利後所洽訂之適用獲利共享協議中所規定。

headings: 與本公司財務狀況相關的風險及對額外資金的需求
自本公司成立以來，我們已產生顯著虧損。我們預期在未來數年內仍將產生虧損，並可能永遠無法實現或維持盈利。
我們從未透過產品銷售產生收入，可能永遠無法實現盈利。
籌措額外資金可能導致股東持股稀釋、限制我們的營運，或要求我們放棄對我們技術或藥物候選品的權利。
本公司有限的營運歷史可能使評估我們迄今為止的業務成功情況及未來可持續性變得困難。
與我們藥物候選品的發現及開發相關的風險
若我們在臨牀試驗中遭遇 enrolment 患者困難或延遲，我們取得必要市場許可的時間可能延遲或無法取得。
藥物製造過程複雜，而我們與我們的第三方製造商在製造努力上仍處於初期階段。
我們可能無法成功達成識別或發現額外潛在藥物候選物的目標，或在進一步擴展我們 DEL-AI 平台的範疇上取得成功。
我們在快速技術變革的環境中面臨著激烈的競爭，這可能會導致他人在我們之前或更成功地發現、開發或商業化產品。
若我們未能在預期的時間內達成預期的開發目標並公告，我們產品的商業化可能會延遲，因而導致我們股票價格下跌。
生技藥品產業受到廣泛的法規義務與政策規範，而這些法規義務與政策可能因司法挑戰而改變。

paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本年度報告表10-K中所有其他資訊，包括「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」一節，以及我們的財務報表與附註說明，以及我們其他公開檔中所載資訊，以決定是否投資本公司普通股。我們無法保證下列所描述的任何事件不會發生。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。我們可能還會面臨其他我們未察覺或認為不重要的風險與不確定性，這些因素可能對我們的業務產生重大負面影響。若任何下列風險發生，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果與未來展望造成重大且負面的影響。在此情況下，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。

我們的淨虧損為2025年11月30日財務年度終了時為264.5 百萬美元，2024年11月30日財務年度終了時為193.6 百萬美元。截至2025年11月30日，我們累計虧損為1,003.2 百萬美元。截至目前為止，我們尚未從產品銷售中產生任何收入，並主要透過合作夥伴及發行本公司權益資產來資助營運。我們目前處於藥物候選品開發的初期階段。我們的領先藥物候選品，bexobrutideg (NX-5948)、zelebrudomide (NX-2127) 和 NX-1607，目前處於臨牀開發的初期階段。我們預期將持續產生重大費用及營運虧損，至少持續數年。我們預期，若我們：
• 增加並進一步發展我們的藥物候選品 bexobrutideg、zelebrudomide 和 NX-1607 的參與人數，並進行第一期與第二期臨牀試驗；
• 提交新藥申請 (INDs) 並啟動其他藥物候選品的臨牀試驗；
• 進入更進階的臨牀開發階段並擴大外部製造能力以供應臨牀試驗；
• 提升我們 DEL-AI 平台的效能，並應用我們的 DEL-AI 平台將更多藥物候選品推進至預臨牀與臨牀開發階段；
